_README: Per-run framework-hyperparameter OVERRIDES for one autoresearch run (e.g. a Phase-3 OFAT trial).
USAGE: copy this to  runs/<task>/<tag>/framework_cfg.json  and keep ONLY the keys you want to override
(delete the rest — any omitted key uses the code default). Copying it verbatim = all defaults = no-op.

INVALID JSON IS A HARD ERROR: every reader goes through tools/run_cfg.py; a file that exists but does not parse raises RunConfigError (budget/timeout guards fail fast) instead of silently reverting to defaults. A missing file or omitted key is fine — malformed JSON is not.

READ BY (tracked code):  semantic_space.py -> the 'space_initialization' section  ·  got_select.py decide -> the 'got' section  ·  semantic_search.py select -> the 'semantic_search' section  ·  slate.py -> the 'judged_slate' section  ·  tune_tools.py select-candidate -> tuner.n_min/top_percentile plus deep-tune allocation  ·  evaluation_budget.py -> deep-tune objective share/per-candidate cap  ·  tuner search scripts -> BO trial/patience controls and elapsed-time receipts · tune_tools.py validate-proposals -> tuner.rewarm_proposals.

PRIORITY: explicit CLI flag (--semantic-policy / --scheduler-policy / --inner-tuner-policy / --catalog / --cfg / --n-min / --top-percentile / --n-trials / --patience) > this file > module fallback. NOTE: BO patience is adaptive by default = min(bo_patience_cap, max(bo_patience_floor, round(1.5*n_dims))); set tuner.bo_patience to force a fixed value.

SETUP: tools/init_run.py persists --dimension-strategy, --llm-intelligence-score, --semantic-policy, --scheduler-policy, --inner-tuner-policy, --max-evaluations, and --timeout here. New experiment runs default to semantic_search.policy=coverage_attempt, tuner.scheduler_policy=anchor_challenger_v1, and tuner.inner_policy=hebo24-hebo20; the resulting 24+10+10 candidate contract uses deep_tune_per_candidate_cap=44. Use the CLI flags to select comparison arms; every 24+20 inner policy (mixup24-turbo20-v1, hebo24-turbo20-v1, and hebo24-hebo20) requires scheduler_policy=anchor_challenger_v1. For a new run without --timeout init_run seeds per_runtime_limit from the task.toml run.timeout_seconds value. Evaluation budget and timeout may change on resume; dimension strategy, semantic policy, scheduler policy, inner tuner policy, and LLM intelligence score cannot change after run artifacts exist — that freeze starts once this file exists, so a run dir pre-seeded with a frozen background but no framework_cfg.json still accepts every flag.

NOTE: the sections below hold the CURRENT DEFAULTS so this doubles as a reference; '_keys' documents each. 'tuner.K' (warm-config count) is read by the tunable-contract-extractor AGENT (not a deterministic tool), but is injectable here too.
runs/ is gitignored, so the copied file is local-only (not committed).

_keys.got.n_seed: outer S-GoT: bootstrap roots before PUCB exploit starts (default 5, equal-budget tuned↑ from 3 — the only robust change). OFAT {2,3,5}.
_keys.got.S: outer: stall threshold → inject B fresh candidates (default 10; fresh count = B, no separate m_fresh). OFAT {5,10,20}.
_keys.got.B: outer: PUCB-generation batch size = candidates per PUCB round (default 2; toy preferred 4 but kept 2 for real-loop cost—4 expensive candidates/round). OFAT {1,2,3}.
_keys.got.C: outer: progressive-widening cap coefficient, cap=ceil(C*N^alpha) (default 1.5). OFAT {1.0,1.5,2.5}.
_keys.got.gamma: outer: c_dag lineage influence decay (default 0.6). OFAT {0.4,0.6,0.8}.
_keys.got.c_pucb: outer: PUCB exploration constant over the action pool (default 0.4; flat in [0.1,0.8], base-dependent → kept default). OFAT {0.2,0.4,0.8}.
_keys.got.c_leaf: outer: select_leaf UCB exploration constant during descent (default 0.4). OFAT {0.2,0.4,0.8}.
_keys.space_initialization.dimension_strategy: search-space setup: catalog_subset selects from contracts/semantic-dimensions-v1.json (default); llm_induced makes background-researcher create and fully use a validated run-local dimension_catalog.json before retrieval. Explicit --catalog overrides the source, not the configured full-vs-subset semantics.
_keys.semantic_search.policy: outer semantic point policy, independent of got graph action selection. New runs default to coverage_attempt. Four deterministic coverage-family arms keep their channels separately attributable: coverage (coverage only), coverage_experience (coverage plus the carrier prior — per-hypothesis independent negative/positive context counts from ledger edges), coverage_attempt (coverage plus the policy-conditioned attempt downside — how candidates previously built at this exact (point, op) turned out under the current policy), and coverage_carrier_attempt (both channels; an interaction arm for checking double counting, not a default). gain, gain_uncertainty, and gain_uncertainty_nocost require per-proposal rubric inputs and preserve background priors, signed experience adjustments, final predicted_gain/uncertainty, cost (absent for gain_uncertainty_nocost), and coverage separately in each record's policy_receipt; they are currently dormant.
_keys.semantic_search.coverage_weight: semantic acquisition: additive deterministic under-coverage contribution for gain policies (default 0.1).
_keys.semantic_search.cost_weight: semantic acquisition: subtractive predicted implementation/evaluation cost contribution (default 0.2).
_keys.semantic_search.uncertainty_weight: semantic acquisition: exploration bonus used only by gain_uncertainty and gain_uncertainty_nocost (default 0.5); uncertainty is a rubric score, not a calibrated posterior.
_keys.semantic_search.deprioritized_budget_int: LEGACY: lane scheduling was removed — deprioritized content is penalized via the carrier prior instead of a reserved selection slot. The key is still accepted (and echoed in schema-6 receipts) but no longer affects selection.
_keys.semantic_search.llm_intelligence_score: pre-run heuristic reliability prior for LLM-authored gain, uncertainty, and cost judgments, on a fixed [0,100] scale (default 100 preserves legacy acquisition exactly; e.g. 44 applies weight 0.44). It is not a calibrated probability or a leaderboard-relative percentile. Deterministic coverage is not scaled, raw forecasts remain unchanged, and score 0 leaves only the configured coverage term even though forecasts are still collected. The applied weight is recorded in policy_receipt. Freeze this value before semantic artifacts exist.
_keys.semantic_search.carrier_pos_weight: experience prior: acquisition bonus per independent positive carrier context for a hypothesis (default 0.05).
_keys.semantic_search.carrier_pos_cap: experience prior: maximum positive contexts counted per hypothesis (default 2).
_keys.semantic_search.carrier_neg_weight: experience prior: acquisition penalty per independent negative carrier context for a hypothesis (default 0.2 — deliberately larger than the positive weight: re-probing a deadend wastes budget, a missed exploration costs nothing measurable).
_keys.semantic_search.carrier_neg_cap: experience prior: maximum negative contexts counted per hypothesis (default 3).
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_noise_threshold: attempt downside: pre-frozen noise threshold tau on the child-minus-parent warm screening delta (default 0.0). |delta| <= tau is screen_neutral, not an improvement. Freeze it before a run — it defines the outcome partition, not a tuning knob.
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_screen_weight: attempt downside: maximum penalty from the screen term (default 0.2). The term fires only on the part of a point's non-improvement rate that exceeds the leave-one-point-out same-op base rate; a success never yields a bonus.
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_crash_weight: attempt downside: maximum penalty from the crash term (default 0.3). A crash is an absolute failure event — it produces a negative value without having to exceed any global crash base rate.
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_screen_prior_str: attempt downside: paired-exposure mass before a point's own failure rate is trusted at full strength (default 2.0). Larger values make early penalties weaker and soft reopening faster.
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_crash_prior_stre: attempt downside: smoothing mass for the absolute crash rate (default 1.0). Strictly positive, so co-occurring unpaired attempts can dilute a crash penalty but never cancel it to exactly zero.
_keys.semantic_search.attempt_cap: attempt downside: floor on the total non-positive adjustment (default 0.6, applied as -0.6) so the channel can flip near-boundary selections without generally overwhelming coverage.
_keys.semantic_search.n_route_sketches: route arm: how many distinct implementation routes the idea generator sketches at the selected point before choosing one (default 0 = no explicit planning step). 1 is the explicit single-route planning baseline, so a 1-vs-3 comparison isolates route breadth rather than the presence of planning. Sketching and choosing happen INSIDE the existing idea-generator invocation — no new role, no extra LLM call. Unrelated to tuner.K. Any value >= 1 makes route provenance mandatory at admission.
_keys.semantic_search.route_memory: route arm: show the generator a bounded, relevance-ordered memory of previously PLANNED routes at or near this point, with each attempt's outcome (default false; requires n_route_sketches >= 1, since memory is shown to a planner). Planned provenance only — it says what was intended, never what the writer actually produced. Enabling it makes route provenance mandatory at admission; missing or inconsistent provenance fails loudly instead of silently degrading into the no-memory arm.
_keys.semantic_search.route_memory_rows: route arm: maximum memory rows shown (default 6). Exact (point_id, op) matches come first, then same-op semantic-assignment neighbors; nearer and newer first.
_keys.semantic_search.route_memory_max_distanc: route arm: how many differing selected assignments still count as a neighbor (default 2). Neighbor rows are transfer context for generation only — they never enter the target point's attempt posterior, which is stratified by exact (point_id, op).
_keys.judged_slate.pool_size: judged-slate arm (semantic_search.policy=judged_slate): how many semantic points the deterministic seating step admits into one generation's judge pool (default 6, integer in [3, 12]; read by tools/slate.py). Slate size and the rollout protocol stay code constants (slate 2, regular rollouts 2, boundary 1). Set it before the run starts; like the semantic policy it is part of the frozen arm definition once run artifacts exist.
_keys.tuner.scheduler_policy: run-global complete-bout scheduler. New experiment runs default to anchor_challenger_v1, the deterministic two-INITIAL/two-DEEP tournament used by the 24+20 policies: early anchor, generation while preserving a hard reserve, late challenger, then two DEEP segments. Its default 24/10/10 tournament reserve is 2*24+10+10=68. v3_2 is the rollout-based comparison arm and requires finite max_evaluations, deep_tune_budget_fraction=null, and deep_tune_per_candidate_cap >= 38 for its four-bout 8+10+10+10 contract. legacy and legacy_wide are the percentile/alternation comparison arms; they differ only in the first-bout non-responder exemption. legacy re-admits only the candidate holding the run-best final score, while legacy_wide re-admits any single-bout non-responder in the top (100-top_percentile)% of the population by best_warm_score. Both cap the retry at one bout and rank it below every waiting responder.
_keys.tuner.inner_policy: regime-conditioned within-bout policy. hebo24-hebo20 (new-experiment default) has two regimes: one 24-slot INITIAL plus up to two scheduler-admitted 10-slot DEEP segments, all using pool_hebo_mace; there is no CONTINUE regime, and the DEEP segment boundary is only for scheduler admission/rescheduling. It has no movable-numeric eligibility gate. Each HEBO step uses an LLM POOL=5 and official HEBO MACE reranking after enough history; before then it executes the proposer's rank-1 point, never pure HEBO or LHS. hebo24-turbo20-v1 keeps that 24-slot HEBO INITIAL but uses two 10-eval candidate-local hot-start TuRBO DEEP segments. mixup24-turbo20-v1 instead uses mixup_pool_hebo for INITIAL and the same two TuRBO DEEP segments. TuRBO moves non-degenerate float and integer dimensions and freezes categoricals, so a candidate with no varying numeric dimension has no DEEP action. deferred-random8-hebo10-spsa10-v1 is the historical v3_2 arm: FIRST = 8 trials with deferred-warm configs followed by explicit Optuna RandomSampler draws, CONTINUE = 10 prompt-v2 HEBO trials, and DEEP = 10 two-sided SPSA evaluations. localtr8-hebo10-spsa10-v1 replaces its FIRST with local_tr; localtr8-hebo10-hebo10-v1 also replaces DEEP with HEBO; selfrank8-hebo10-hebo10 uses LLM-pool self-rank for FIRST and HEBO later. Regime-conditioned policies take no re-warm proposals. legacy is the pre-policy uniform behavior at tuner.bout_trials, with deferred configs extending the bout.
_keys.tuner.scheduler_scenarios: scheduler v3.2 paired rollout scenario count (default 64); recorded in every scheduler decision receipt.
_keys.tuner.max_bouts_per_candidate: scheduler v3.2 maximum complete bouts per candidate (default 4). Together with bout_trials this is the scheduler's per-candidate resource contract.
_keys.tuner.K: inner: number of warm-start configs the tunable-contract-extractor PROPOSES per candidate (default 5; read by the AGENT; settable per run with driver run --k-warm / init_run.py --k-warm, frozen once run artifacts exist). K − K_eval of them are DEFERRED, so this is the knob that sets the deferred-config count. OFAT {3,5,8} — highest-impact inner knob.
_keys.tuner.K_eval: inner: how many of the K proposed warm configs are uniformly sampled without replacement and EVALUATED at step 0+1 (default 2, minimum 2; best-of-K_eval = screening score). Was 3; lowered because screening is where budget goes to die — run 0802-sonnet-ex125-1 spent 74 of 124 evaluations on it for zero score improvements. 2 is the floor that still gives a non-fresh candidate one inherited fidelity control plus one selectable treatment row. Also raises got_select's admission cap floor(remaining/max(2,K_eval)), so fewer slots end up unspendable at the end of a run. The sampled permutation is persisted in tune_report.phase_a.warm_config_selection for exact resume; list order has no screening priority. The remaining K−K_eval are DEFERRED — stored params-only in tune_report.phase_a.deferred_configs and evaluated only if the candidate is promoted. They occupy slots inside the INITIAL bout: 24 under the default hebo24-hebo20 policy; the historical v3_2 comparison policy calls its 8-slot initialization FIRST. Under legacy they extend the bout. K_eval>=K disables deferral (evaluate all).
_keys.tuner.n_min: inner: min population before deep-tune fires. NOW DERIVED from top_percentile = ceil(100/(100-P)) (P=80→5); this key is only an explicit OVERRIDE.
_keys.tuner.top_percentile: inner: deep-tune eligibility — best untuned must rank in the top (100-P)% (default 80). OFAT {70,80,90}.
_keys.tuner.bo_n_trials: inner: Phase-C BO trial budget (default 40, raised from 30 per benchmark).
_keys.tuner.bo_patience_cap: inner: cap for the ADAPTIVE BO patience = min(cap, max(12, round(1.5*n_dims))) (default cap 20). low/mid-dim save budget, high-dim ramps to cap. benchmark: ~94% of fixed-20's gain at ~64% cost.
_keys.tuner.bo_patience: inner: OPTIONAL fixed-patience override; if set, disables the adaptive rule above. omit for adaptive. (patience=6 was the main HPO suppressor — don't go below ~12.)
_keys.tuner.bo_patience_floor: inner: floor for adaptive patience (default 12 — must clear the ~startup random period or HPO gets 0).
_keys.tuner.deep_tune_budget_fraction: inner budget policy: OPTIONAL maximum fraction of max_evaluations that Phase C may reserve across the run. DEFAULT null = NO run-level cap. The former 0.4 default was underived and actively harmful: in run 0802-sonnet-ex125-1 it bound at evaluation 87 of 124, and all 37 evaluations after it went to screening — which produced zero score improvements for the whole run, while both improvements came from Phase C. Three later candidates landed within noise of the incumbent and none could be tuned. Same failure shape as the removed wall clock (see deep_tune_time_limit_seconds): a ceiling on the productive mechanism, chosen without measurement. Set an explicit fraction only with run evidence justifying it; 0 disables deep tuning entirely. Per-candidate bounding is deep_tune_per_candidate_cap, which is still on by default. NAMED TRADE-OFF: with no run-level share, Phase C can consume nearly the entire budget (bounded only by the per-candidate cap times the number of promoted candidates), screening gets whatever Phase C leaves, and no run-level wall-clock guard exists — this governance loosening is deliberate per the run evidence above, not an oversight.
_keys.tuner.deep_tune_per_candidate_cap: inner budget policy: maximum admitted Phase-C objective calls for one candidate across all its bouts and retries. Default 44 is the exact hebo24-hebo20 lifetime (24+10+10). The other 24+20 policies require the same cap. Under scheduler_policy=v3_2 the cap must be at least its 38-call lifetime (8+10+10+10).
_keys.tuner.bout_trials: inner: LEGACY-policy objective-attempt budget of one tuning bout (default 10). Regime-conditioned policies ignore this size: the default hebo24-hebo20 schedule is 24/10/10, while the historical v3_2 regime policy is 8/10/10/10. The orchestrator's per-invocation trial cap is min(policy bout size, per-candidate-cap remaining, budget remaining).
_keys.tuner.tuned_threshold: inner: cumulative Phase-C attempts at which a candidate's evaluation_depth becomes 'tuned' (default 20 = two full bouts); 1..threshold-1 attempts is 'tuned_lightly', 0 is 'screening'.
_keys.tuner.rewarm_proposals: inner: maximum number of warm configs the tuner-orchestrator may PROPOSE at a CONTINUE bout (default 3). Regime-conditioned policies, including the default hebo24-hebo20, do not use this path: HEBO generates its own pool and SPSA requires complete pairs. Only the legacy policy still accepts orchestrator re-warm proposals.
_keys.tuner.deep_tune_time_limit_seconds: REMOVED — accepted for backward compatibility but ignored. A cumulative Phase-C wall-clock cap (former default 3600) silently degraded BO to random search whenever the cap afforded fewer trials than the sampler's startup regime (3600s at ~450s/eval < TPE's 10 startup trials). Phase-C budget is now trial-denominated: tuner.bo_n_trials, adaptive patience, tuner.deep_tune_per_candidate_cap, and tuner.deep_tune_budget_fraction; per_runtime_limit still bounds each single evaluation.
_keys.max_evaluations: OPTIONAL strict global objective budget = max calls admitted into the task config->score fn. Every tuner atomically reserves one slot in evaluation_attempts.jsonl immediately before score_fn; once the cap is reached no further score call starts, even mid-round or mid-tuner. trials_attempted includes successful and failed admitted score calls; preflight attempts/rejections are reported separately and never consume objective slots. Legacy records without trials_attempted fall back to trials_completed and then warm_start_K.
_keys.per_runtime_limit: OPTIONAL per-evaluation wall-clock limit in SECONDS (one evaluate_config / one train.py run). A config/run exceeding it is hard-killed and recorded as a failed/crashed trial. Enforced by the eval callers, not prepare.py: framework tuners (warmstart_eval/bo/cmaes) run each eval in a timed subprocess; hillclimb uses timed_run.py. The template fallback is 60, but init_run seeds a new real task run from task.toml run.timeout_seconds unless --timeout explicitly overrides it. null/absent = no limit. THIS VALUE IS TASK-SPECIFIC — set it after measuring the task's heaviest legitimate candidate.
_keys.preflight_runtime_limit: OPTIONAL per-config no-score preflight timeout in seconds. Preflight may import/construct a candidate and execute the task-owned smoke hook, but it never calls score_fn or consumes max_evaluations. Defaults to min(180, per_runtime_limit) when omitted.
